subject: Government
title: Early Nigerian Constitutions (1922–1954)
outline: Features, merits and demerits of each
Growth of the elective principle and regionalism

modules.title: Clifford (1922) and Richards (1946)
modules.html:
1. Clifford Constitution, 1922

  • Introduced the elective principle for the first time in British West Africa.
  • Legislative Council of 46 members with 4 elected Africans — 3 for Lagos and 1 for Calabar.
  • Franchise restricted to adult males with a gross annual income of £100 and twelve months' residence.
  • Legislative Council legislated for the Colony and Southern Provinces only; the Governor legislated for the North by proclamation.
  • Provided for a Nigerian Council abolition and encouraged party formation — the NNDP (1923) was formed to contest the seats.

Merits: birth of elective politics, parties and a nationalist press. Demerits: tiny franchise, North excluded, official majority, purely advisory African role.

2. Richards Constitution, 1946

  • Introduced regionalism: three regions — Northern, Western and Eastern — each with a Regional House of Assembly (and a House of Chiefs in the North).
  • Brought the North into a single central Legislative Council for the first time, promoting unity in a formal sense.
  • Increased unofficial African membership, but members were largely nominated by Native Authorities rather than elected.
  • Regional houses were advisory, with no legislative power of their own.

Merits: unified North and South legislatively; recognised regional diversity; enlarged African participation. Demerits: imposed without consultation ('a constitution imposed by an autocrat', said the nationalists); retained official majority; nomination instead of election; sowed the seeds of divisive regionalism. Nationalist opposition led to its replacement after only a few years.

examples.q: Why is 1922 regarded as the beginning of party politics in Nigeria?
examples.a: Because Clifford's four elective seats created, for the first time, an electoral prize worth organising for. Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP in 1923 to contest the Lagos seats, which it won repeatedly until 1938. Parties, campaigns and a partisan press (the Lagos Daily News) followed directly from the elective principle.

examples.q: Assess the claim that the Richards Constitution 'united Nigeria to divide it'.
examples.a: It united the country by bringing the North into one central Legislative Council for the first time, ending the constitutional separation dating from 1914. Yet by creating three regions with their own houses and identities, and by using nominated Native Authority representatives, it institutionalised regional consciousness and gave ambitious politicians regional power bases — the structural root of the tripolar rivalry of the First Republic.

modules.title: Macpherson (1951) and Lyttelton (1954)
modules.html:
1. Macpherson Constitution, 1951

  • Preceded by wide consultation from village to national level — the most participatory process to that date.
  • Created a Central Council of Ministers with African members drawn from the regions.
  • Regional Houses acquired real legislative powers subject to central assent, and regional executive councils were established.
  • Central legislature: a 148-member House of Representatives, mainly elected indirectly through regional houses.
  • Unofficial majority achieved; ministers had portfolios but no full responsibility.

Reasons for collapse: ministers lacked collective responsibility and could not control policy; regional members owed loyalty to their regions rather than the centre; the 1953 Anthony Enahoro motion for self-government in 1956 was resisted by the North, provoking the walk-out of Northern members and the Kano riots of May 1953; the Eastern Region crisis of 1953 ('sit-tight ministers') paralysed the constitution.

2. The 1953 London and 1954 Lagos Conferences

Convened by Oliver Lyttelton, Secretary of State for the Colonies, they agreed on a federal structure, regional self-government for those regions that wanted it, and the separation of Lagos as federal territory.

3. Lyttelton Constitution, 1954

  • Established a genuine federation — the first true federal constitution in Nigeria.
  • Divided powers into exclusive, concurrent and residual lists.
  • Regions gained autonomy in their spheres and could become self-governing separately — the West and East did so in 1957, the North in 1959.
  • Lagos became federal territory; the Southern Cameroons became a quasi-federal territory.
  • Direct election to the House of Representatives (184 seats) in most regions; the Governor-General remained head of the central executive.
  • Regionalised the public service, judiciary and marketing boards.

Merits: laid the federal foundation on which independence was built; reduced inter-regional friction; allowed differential pace of development. Demerits: strengthened regionalism and regional parties, weakened the centre, and left the minorities question unresolved — hence the Willink Commission of 1957.

examples.q: Trace the events that destroyed the Macpherson Constitution.
examples.a: In March 1953 Anthony Enahoro of the Action Group moved that Nigeria attain self-government in 1956. Northern members, fearing domination by the more educated South, opposed it and tabled 'as soon as practicable'; AG and NCNC members jeered them, and Northern delegates were abused in Lagos. The North then tabled an eight-point programme close to confederation, and the Kano riots of May 1953 followed a Southern political tour. Simultaneously the Eastern Region crisis over ministers who refused to resign paralysed the regional executive. These deadlocks forced the London Conference of 1953 and the constitution's replacement in 1954.

examples.q: Why is the Lyttelton Constitution regarded as Nigeria's first genuinely federal constitution?
examples.a: Because it did what its predecessors did not: it divided legislative power between the centre and the regions by an exclusive, concurrent and residual list scheme, gave each region its own executive, legislature, public service, judiciary and marketing board, and made neither level the creature of the other. Regions could attain internal self-government independently of one another — real constitutional autonomy rather than devolved advice.

modules.title: Features, merits and demerits of each
modules.html:
Features, merits and demerits of each is a key part of Early Nigerian Constitutions (1922–1954) (SSS 3, Government). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Merits: birth of elective politics, parties and a nationalist press.
  • Demerits: tiny franchise, North excluded, official majority, purely advisory African role.
  • Merits: unified North and South legislatively; recognised regional diversity; enlarged African participation.
  • Demerits: imposed without consultation ('a constitution imposed by an autocrat', said the nationalists); retained official majority; nomination instead of election; sowed the seeds of divisive regionalism.
  • Merits: laid the federal foundation on which independence was built; reduced inter-regional friction; allowed differential pace of development.

Worked example

Q: The elective principle was introduced in Nigeria by the:
A: Clifford Constitution — Clifford's 1922 constitution created four elective seats.

Q: Under the Clifford Constitution voters needed an annual income of:
A: £100 — The franchise was restricted to adult males earning £100 gross per annum.

quiz.q: The elective principle was introduced in Nigeria by the:
quiz.solution: Clifford's 1922 constitution created four elective seats.

quiz.q: Under the Clifford Constitution voters needed an annual income of:
quiz.solution: The franchise was restricted to adult males earning £100 gross per annum.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution came into force in:
quiz.solution: Sir Arthur Richards's constitution took effect in 1946.

quiz.q: Regionalism was formally introduced by the:
quiz.solution: Richards created three regions with advisory Houses of Assembly.

quiz.q: A major criticism of the Richards Constitution was that it was:
quiz.solution: Nationalists condemned the absence of consultation and the nomination of members.

quiz.q: The most widely consulted of the early constitutions was the:
quiz.solution: Macpherson's constitution followed consultation from village to national level.

quiz.q: The self-government motion of 1953 was moved by:
quiz.solution: Enahoro of the Action Group moved for self-government in 1956.

quiz.q: The Kano riots occurred in:
quiz.solution: The riots of May 1953 followed the self-government motion crisis.

quiz.q: Nigeria's first genuinely federal constitution was the:
quiz.solution: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution established a federation with legislative lists.

quiz.q: Under the 1954 Constitution, Lagos became:
quiz.solution: Lagos was separated as federal territory.

quiz.q: The Western and Eastern Regions attained internal self-government in:
quiz.solution: Both became self-governing in 1957; the North followed in 1959.

quiz.q: Powers in the 1954 Constitution were divided into:
quiz.solution: This threefold division is the hallmark of Nigerian federalism.

quiz.q: The 1953 constitutional conference held in:
quiz.solution: The London conference of 1953 agreed on federal principles; Lagos followed in 1954.

quiz.q: The commission on minority fears set up in 1957 was the:
quiz.solution: The Willink Commission examined and reported on minority fears in 1958.

quiz.q: Under the Clifford Constitution the North was:
quiz.solution: The Legislative Council covered only the Colony and Southern Provinces.

quiz.q: A weakness of the Macpherson Constitution was:
options: Absence of collective responsibility among ministers
quiz.solution: Ministers had portfolios but no collective responsibility, leading to deadlock.

quiz.q: The 1922 Clifford Constitution allowed for how many elected Africans?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 4.

quiz.q: The 1954 Lyttleton constitution is best known for?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Formally establishing federalism in Nigeria.

quiz.q: The primary reason for the 1953 London Constitutional Conference was?
options: To settle regional differences following the 1953 self-govt crisis
To elect a President for Nigeria
To sign a trade treaty with France
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: To settle regional differences following the 1953 self-govt crisis.

quiz.q: The 1979 Constitution was modeled after the?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: American Presidential system.

quiz.q: Which of these is a defining feature of the 1979 Constitution?
options: Traditional rulers as heads of state
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Introduction of an Executive President.

quiz.q: The 1960 Independence Constitution provided for a?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Ceremonial Queen (as Head of State).

quiz.q: The ‘Age of Enlightenment’ in Europe primarily influenced the growth of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Modern Democracy.

quiz.q: A constitution that is easy to change or amend is called?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Flexible.

quiz.q: What is a ‘Constitution’?
options: A body of fundamental principles and laws
A history book of a nation
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: A body of fundamental principles and laws.

quiz.q: The ‘Zikist Movement’ in the 1940s was known for being?
options: Radical and militant in its nationalism
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Radical and militant in its nationalism.

quiz.q: A ‘Vote of No Confidence’ is a tool used for?
options: Removing the government in a parliamentary system
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Removing the government in a parliamentary system.

quiz.q: The symbolic head of the Commonwealth is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: The British Monarch.

quiz.q: In what year did the Aba Women's War (Riot) occur?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 1929.

quiz.q: The NYM was formed in 1934. What does NYM stand for?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Nigerian Youth Movement.

quiz.q: How many states were created by General Yakubu Gowon in 1967?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 12.

quiz.q: The leader of the Northern People’s Congress (NPC) was?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Ahmadu Bello.

quiz.q: The ‘Ali-must-go’ student protest of 1978 was primarily over?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Education costs and welfare.

quiz.q: The annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election was won by?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: M.K.O. Abiola.

quiz.q: The African Union (AU) formally replaced the OAU in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 2002.

quiz.q: The primary goal of ECOWAS is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Economic integration and cooperation.

quiz.q: Which UN agency is primarily responsible for global health?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: WHO.

quiz.q: The Commonwealth of Nations consists mostly of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Former British colonies.

quiz.q: The current Secretary-General of the United Nations (as of 2024) is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Antonio Guterres.

quiz.q: OPEC is an international organization primarily concerned with?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Petroleum/Oil.

quiz.q: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was formed during the?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Cold War.

quiz.q: The headquarters of ECOWAS is located in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Abuja.

quiz.q: ‘ECOMOG’ is the military intervention arm of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: ECOWAS.

quiz.q: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) consists of how many judges?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 15.

quiz.q: The term ‘Third World’ traditionally refers to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Developing nations.

quiz.q: Which country hosted the founding meeting of the OAU in 1963?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Ethiopia.

quiz.q: The United Nations (UN) was founded in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 1945.

quiz.q: What does UNICEF stand for?
options: United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund
Union of Nations for International Children
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund.

quiz.q: The term ‘New World Order’ became prominent in global politics after the?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Cold War.

quiz.q: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) primarily provides?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Financial loans and economic advice.
